**Six fixes at the cause, and the seventh measured and stopped — broken 32 → 23 on the six named pages (−28%), and not one contrast finding is classed broken any more.** 18 shots, $1.57 (ceiling $2), sonnet `critique-full-v1`. ![/framework/ui/ @1280, after](/framework/ai/2026-08-17/layout-wave-3/ui-1280-after.png) | page | 390 | 1280 | 3440 | before → after | |---|---|---|---|---| | `/framework/core/Page/doc/` | 2→2 | 2→1 | 1→0 | **5 → 3** | | `/framework/ui/` | 2→2 | 2→1 | 2→2 | **6 → 5** | | `/framework/ai/` | 2→1 | 1→1 | 2→2 | **5 → 4** | | `/web/` | 1→0 | 2→1 | 2→2 | **5 → 3** | | `mastermind-shots` | 2→2 | 2→1 | 2→2 | **6 → 5** | | `/framework/styles/layouts/` | 2→1 | 2→0 | 1→2 | **5 → 3** | ## The one I stopped on — [the write-up](/framework/ai/2026-08-17/layout-wave-3/proposal.md) Built the subgrid pass-through on `.flow` and measured it at three widths on both named pages: **not one pixel moved.** The word was already reachable — **nothing claims it**, because `md()` emits raw marked output with no classes at all. Injecting the *claim* instead is **one word in `AITask.js:76`** (`"ai-task flow wide"`), needs no Page.css rule, and takes `mastermind-shots` @3440 from 720px tables in a 2,986px page to **2,806px**, and the page from 5,538px tall to **2,425px**. Outside this task's fence — Mike's call. ## What landed, one line each - **Every card wears the surface** (`Page.css`) — the `:not(:has(> .page-preview-thumb))` guard deleted. The sweep's second-largest cluster (38 findings) was one selector: a thumbed card went bare, so its caption read as a heading for the empty row below. - **`.muted` 65% → 75%** (`framework.css`) — #828282 **3.84:1** / #7e7e7e **3.63:1** → #6f6f6f **5.02:1** / #6c6c6c **4.69:1**, over AA on white and `--wash`, in 253 call sites. Contrast findings on these six pages: 3 broken → **0**. - **`--subtle`: no change, and that is the finding.** Wave 2's `framework.css` bump never reached a pixel — `lew42.css:18` overrides `:root`. The theme's own `#6a6a6a` is **5.41:1 / 4.83:1**, already darker than the bump's `#737373` (4.74:1 / 4.62:1). Both files now carry the ratios. - **The tab strip fades at both ends** (`tabs.css`) — the left fade is exactly `--tab-pad-x`, so an unscrolled strip loses one tab's padding and no glyph. - **Inline `code` is a wash, not a dark pill** (`framework.css`) — `pre` and `code` split their backgrounds; `--code-bg` now means the block. 9.41:1, up from the pill's 8.44:1. - **`--prim-ink`** — the accent's text twin, `light-dark(#B84A24, #FF8F60)`: **2.25:1 → 5.19:1** on white, 2.01:1 → 4.64:1 on `--wash`. A token that defaults to `--prim`; every fill, outline and active bar still says `--prim`. - **`--pad-y: clamp(1.5em, 4%, 3em)`** — 42px → **21px** at 390, 45 → 42 at 1280, 54px unchanged at 3440. ## Rejected, with the measurement - **`auto-fit` on `.wall`** — injected site-wide it made `/web/`'s two cards **583px each at 1280 and 1,623px each at 3440**, which is what `Page.css:186` has warned since the word landed. And an empty track is what a `--column`-sized wall *is*: the sweep's own prompt feedback #5 says so. - **The table rule the sweep asked for already exists** — `framework.css:278`, with its own measurement in the comment. Cluster #5 is stale. ## Left - **Width at 3440 is still the whole remaining story** — 8 of the 23 broken findings, on all six pages. It is what step 1 stopped on, and it is authoring, not CSS. - **The tab strip: 3 broken, unchanged.** Two of the three are about the *right* edge, which has carried a 2em fade since wave 2, and one of them writes "SESSI…" — describing the fade while calling it a clip. Widening the left fade past `--tab-pad-x` would dim the first label of every unscrolled tab bar on the site to fix an intermittent cut. Prompt feedback, not CSS. - **`/framework/ui/` @3440 "cards have no visible border"** — the border is there; `--line` `#e6e6e6` on `#ffffff` is imperceptible in a downscaled 3440 shot. A theme decision. - **Clusters #10–#14** (66 findings) — affordance and component JS, fenced out. #11, `--flow` flat so an `h2` gets a `
